sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Types / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: Which part of the foot is primarily recommended for executing a highly accurate short pass in Football?
options: B) The outside of the foot
C) The inside of the foot
questions.answer: C) The inside of the foot

questions.question_text: How many active players are permitted on the mat for a single team during competitive Kabaddi gameplay?
True or False: A football player is allowed to score a goal by throwing the ball directly into the net from a throw-in.
questions.answer: B) False

questions.question_text: In Kabaddi, a 'Super Tackle' is executed and awards 2 points when the defending team successfully traps the raider with how many defenders on the mat?
questions.answer: C) 3 or fewer defenders

questions.question_text: Which foundational Yoga posture is widely known as the 'Tree Pose'?
questions.answer: B) Vrikshasana

questions.question_text: In Football, what action is taken when a defensive player deliberately kicks the ball over their own goal line?
options: A) Goal kick for the defense
B) Corner kick for the attacking team
questions.answer: B) Corner kick for the attacking team

questions.question_text: Under Kabaddi rules, the bonus line is active and grants a point to the raider only when the defending team has a minimum of how many players on the mat?
questions.answer: C) 6 players

questions.question_text: True or False: In Yoga, Pranayama refers exclusively to physical flexibility exercises and not breathing techniques.
questions.answer: B) False

questions.question_text: Which defensive technique is commonly used in Football to legally steal the ball from an opponent without committing a foul?
questions.answer: B) Block tackling

questions.question_text: True or False: The sequence of Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation) comprises a continuous flow of exactly 12 specific postures.
questions.answer: A) True

questions.question_text: Explain the fundamental purpose of 'dribbling' in a competitive football match. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Dribbling allows a player to maintain possession of the ball while moving rapidly across the field, maneuvering past defenders using short, controlled foot taps.

questions.question_text: Define a 'Lona' in Kabaddi and state its specific point value. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A Lona is awarded when an entire defending team is declared out. The opposing team receives two additional points, and the dismissed team is fully revived.

questions.question_text: Identify two distinct physical benefits of regularly practicing Tadasana (Mountain Pose). [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Regular practice of Tadasana corrects bodily alignment and posture, strengthens the ankles and knees, and increases overall spinal stability and vertical balance.

questions.question_text: Describe a 'throw-in' in football and specify when it is awarded. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A throw-in restarts play after the ball completely crosses the touchline. It is awarded to the opponents of the player who last touched the ball.

questions.question_text: Briefly outline the defensive role of the 'anti' in a game of Kabaddi. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The 'anti' works cooperatively within a chain formation to anticipate the raider's footwork, prevent them from scoring touch points, and execute physical tackles.

questions.question_text: Explain the rules governing a valid 'Cant' during an offensive raid sequence in a competitive Kabaddi match. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The raider must begin chanting the word 'Kabaddi' clearly in a single continuous breath before entering the opponent's court. If they lose the chant or pause for breath inside the boundary, they are declared out.

questions.question_text: Describe the correct biomechanical technique for executing a push pass to a teammate in Football. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Plant the non-kicking foot firmly beside the ball, pointing at the target. Turn the kicking foot outward, lock the ankle, and strike the center of the ball with the inside of the foot, following through smoothly.

questions.question_text: How does the practice of Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose) positively affect a student's respiratory and muscular systems? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Bhujangasana expands the chest cavity, significantly improving lung capacity and respiratory efficiency. Simultaneously, it deeply stretches the abdominal muscles and strengthens the spine, relieving upper and lower back stiffness caused by poor sitting posture.

questions.question_text: Outline the tactical advantage of forming a 'chain' while defending against an aggressive raider in Kabaddi. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Forming a chain by holding hands allows defenders to move cohesively as a unit, trapping the raider in a semi-circle. It provides mutual physical support, severely restricting the raider's escape routes back to the midline.

questions.question_text: Analyze how executing structural postures in Yoga helps a student football player lower muscle fatigue and prevent common on-field hyper-extension injuries. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Yoga asanas build deep structural flexibility by elongating tight muscle groups like hamstrings and calves. Holding controlled balancing postures increases core stability and joint coordination. This protects the player's knees during sudden directional cuts on the pitch, while deep breath management channels oxygen to tissues, drastically reducing localized lactic acid accumulation and fatigue.

questions.question_text: Formulate a defensive strategy for a Kabaddi team that currently has only three players left on the mat, aiming to successfully execute a 'Super Tackle'. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: With only three defenders remaining, the team must maintain a tight, close-knit chain deep within their half to prevent the raider from securing easy touch points. They must patiently bait the raider into stepping too deep, then simultaneously execute a coordinated ankle hold and torso block, using combined body leverage to pin the raider.
